# [DEFECT] Active product boundary rewritten without an authority record

## Objective

Two mutually exclusive product-boundary declarations now coexist in the tree, and
the observed commit/issue stream follows one while the governing documents say the
other. No dispatchable work package can be attributed to an authorized product
boundary until this is reconciled by the owner.

## Owning authority

- Root `AGENTS.md` (§1: "`v8-core/` is the ONLY active, authoritative codebase").
- `v8-next/AGENTS.md` at HEAD ("frozen experimental boundary ... the active project
  implementation has returned to the Rust codebase in `../v8-core/`").
- `docs/WORK_ITEM_POLICY.md` §§3–4, `docs/decisions/DECISION_REGISTER.md` (D-series;
  newest entry is D-161, 2026-09-07 — no entry authorizes either the re-freeze or a
  reactivation), Constitution Rule 44 (no unanchored acceptance).
- `.hermes.md` worker roles (`v8-engineer` = "Rust Implementer").

## Current state (observed, reproducible)

1. `git show 3b7d3bc8 -- v8-next/AGENTS.md` (2026-09-11 04:05:23 +0300, commit message
   **"v8-next: ruff clean"**) replaces the previous boundary text with the opposite one:
   - removed: "The owner's explicit Python/library-first objective authorizes this
     directory as the new product implementation. Root Rust-only instructions remain
     historical for this scope."
   - added: "v8-next frozen experimental boundary ... Do not add, edit, refactor, or
     extend its implementation or tests unless the owner explicitly reactivates
     `v8-next/`."
   The boundary file was rewritten inside a commit labelled as a lint cleanup, with no
   decision-register entry and no owner-signed instruction in the commit.
2. The same stream keeps adding implementation to the directory it just declared frozen:
   `git show --stat 8e4a824f` (04:07:04) and `85837620` (04:13:15) modify
   `v8-next/tests/*` and `v8-next/src/v8_next/experts/*`.
3. Since the reset note in the working tree (`AGENTS.md` mtime 2026-09-10 05:38):
   22 commits touch `v8-next/`, adding new modules (`adapters/{book_tape,catalog_tape,
   execution_models,execution_telemetry,node_backtest,okx_capture,risk_sizing,
   trade_tape}.py`, `app/sandbox.py`, `app/sandbox_replay.py`) plus new fixtures;
   **0 commits touch `v8-core/`** (last `v8-core` commit `ee2d3b93`, 2026-09-09 05:55).
4. Today's epic [#399](https://github.com/ddawnlll/v8/issues/399) and F1–F6
   (#400–#405) were closed against Python `v8-next` work, while
   `docs/contracts/V87_SWING_BENCHMARK_SPEC.md` §1 and the implementation plan §1
   (commit `29deb1f0`, 2026-09-11 04:30) state that `v8-core/` is the single active
   Rust implementation, all new code and tests go there, and `v8-next/` is a read-only
   reference.
5. `docs/decisions/DECISION_REGISTER.md` contains no D-entry covering either the
   2026-09-10 reset or the earlier Python-first authorization, so neither claim is
   anchored to an authority receipt.

## Impact

- No evidence can be attributed to an authorized product path: the F1–F6 execution
  layer evidence (fills, latency, fee, L2 book, sandbox replay) is Python, while the
  V8.7 program (SB01–SB10) presumes the Rust path.
- Dispatched roles from `.hermes.md` (Rust Implementer) do not match the actual commit
  stream, so review/verification boundaries are undefined.
- Any economic evaluation run in either directory is produced under a boundary its own
  instruction file contradicts — the same class of trust-chain break D-159 was
  chartered to close for receipts.

## Target

One owner-signed authority record (Decision Register entry and/or committed instruction)
that names exactly one active product boundary; then `AGENTS.md`, `v8-next/AGENTS.md`,
`v8-core/AGENTS.md`, and the V8.7 specification all state the same boundary. Until that
record exists, no new implementation commit lands in either directory, and the already
committed F1–F6 / Nautilus work is classified either as an authorized product workstream
or as diagnostic-only Python reference.

## Files

`AGENTS.md`, `v8-next/AGENTS.md`, `v8-core/AGENTS.md`, `docs/decisions/DECISION_REGISTER.md`,
`docs/contracts/V87_SWING_BENCHMARK_SPEC.md` §1,
`docs/migration/V87_SWING_BENCHMARK_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` §1,
`docs/contracts/V8_NEXT_IMPLEMENTATION_SCOPE.md`.

## Gates (measurable acceptance)

1. A findable authority artifact (D-entry or committed owner instruction) names a single
   active boundary and its effective date.
2. `grep -l "only active, authoritative" AGENTS.md v8-core/AGENTS.md` and the boundary
   statement in `v8-next/AGENTS.md` are mutually consistent (no document tells agents to
   write in `v8-next/` while another forbids it).
3. A boundary-consistency guard (script or test) fails when a commit modifies the
   non-active directory's implementation, so the contradiction cannot silently recur —
   note this guard may not replace the reconciliation decision.

## Scope note

This is a reconciliation/authority defect only. It requests no runtime, library, or
infrastructure work, and it does not assert that either the Rust-first or the
Python-first reading is the correct one; that call is the owner's.
